stem.text: Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid according to the following equation.

items: A $3.27\,\text{g}$ sample of zinc reacts with an excess of hydrochloric acid to give $0.0500\,\text{mol}$ of zinc chloride.
A $6.54\,\text{g}$ sample of zinc reacts completely with exactly $100\,\text{cm}^{3}$ of $1.00\,\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ hydrochloric acid.
A $13.08\,\text{g}$ sample of zinc reacts with an excess of hydrochloric acid to give $9.60\,\text{dm}^{3}$ of hydrogen, measured at room conditions.
